articles.title: The Dead Sea has been building a salt floor for years; scientists reveal how it happens
articles.description: Scientists have uncovered a double diffusion process explaining Dead Sea salt accumulation. Warm, salty upper waters interact with cooler, less salty layers below. This creates salt fingers which carry salt downwards to the lakebed. Numerical simulations confirmed this asymmetric fingering mechanism drives salt deposition. This process explains the continuous thickening of the Dead Sea floor with salt.

articles.title: Ramayana timeline explained: Why the epic’s story, manuscripts and artworks may belong to different eras
articles.description: The Ramayana may not have a single historical date, with its story, written manuscripts and artwork emerging in different periods, according to mythologist Devdutt Pattanaik. He estimates the underlying story to be around 3,000 years old, the manuscripts about 2,000 years old and the earliest artwork roughly 1,500 years old.

Five years later, Ayaan triumphed over his battle, emerging cancer-free.

articles.title: Google’s India-first AI models for agriculture are finding applications beyond India
articles.description: Google's agricultural AI models, developed in India, have expanded their reach to eleven countries, facilitating advancements in farming and water management systems. By harnessing satellite imagery, these models support sustainable practices, such as rice cultivation and informed agricultural financing. State governments are now incorporating this innovative technology into their digital agriculture platforms, ultimately enhancing global food security through improved data access.
